questions.question:
Determine the crane's gross capacity based on the following configuration:

• Outriggers fully extended — 24 ft spread (100%)
• Counterweight — 18,000 lb
• 360° rotation
• Main boom — 41.3 ft, fully retracted
• Radius — 10 ft
• Swingaway stowed

options.explanation: Incorrect. 24,000 lb is the counterweight install/remove table on the load-handling page (LMI #0801), not the main 100% chart.

Correct. Main boom chart, 41.3–128 ft, 18,000 lb counterweight, 100% / 24 ft / 360°. At 10 ft on the 41.3 ft column the capacity is 160,000 lb (boom angle 71°). Ten parts of line are required for this cell.
Incorrect. 150,000 lb is the 41.3 ft column at 12 ft, not 10 ft.
Incorrect. 124,000 lb is the 50 ft boom at 10–15 ft. Wrong boom-length column.

questions.question:
Determine the crane's net capacity based on the following configuration:

• Outriggers fully extended — 24 ft spread (100%)
• Counterweight — 18,000 lb
• 360° rotation
• Main boom — 41.3 ft, fully retracted
• Radius — 10 ft
• Swingaway stowed
• 80 USt 5-sheave hook block — 1,319 lb
• Rigging — 200 lb

options.explanation: Incorrect. That is the gross chart capacity. Net = gross − hook block − rigging.
Incorrect. That only subtracts the 1,319 lb block. Deduct the 200 lb of rigging as well.
Correct. Gross at 41.3 ft / 10 ft is 160,000 lb. Stowed swingaway has no deduct. 160,000 − 1,319 − 200 = 158,481 lb.
Incorrect. That subtracts the 3,700 lb erected 33 ft extension. The swingaway is stowed — the chart says no deduct for a stowed boom extension.

options.explanation: Incorrect. At 45 ft the 90 ft column is 22,700 lb — below 25,000 lb. Never interpolate and never use a cell that is short.
Incorrect. 42 ft is not a listed radius. When the radius is between listed values, use the next longer listed radius.
Correct. 90 ft column: 35 ft = 31,350 lb (ok), 40 ft = 27,500 lb (ok), 45 ft = 22,700 lb (short). Never interpolate. Maximum listed radius that still holds 25,000 lb is 40 ft.
Incorrect. At 50 ft the 90 ft column is 22,450 lb.

options.text: No reduction — the chart only deducts when lifting on the extension

Correct. Weight reductions for load handling devices: 33 ft extension erected — 3,700 lb reduction of main-boom capacities. 56 ft erected is 7,830 lb. No deduct for a stowed boom extension.
Incorrect. 7,830 lb is the 56 ft extension erected, not the 33 ft.
Incorrect. 136 lb is the auxiliary boom nose, not the erected swingaway.

Incorrect. Four parts is far below 160,000 lb on this hoist.
Correct. The 10 ft / 160,000 lb cell is marked ++ : ten parts of line required, using the auxiliary boom nose. See the operator's handbook reeving diagram.
Incorrect. Single-part line pull on this hoist is 16,800 lb.

questions.question: The planned radius is 33 ft. The 39.4 ft boom chart lists 30 ft and 35 ft, not 33 ft. Which radius do you use?

options.explanation: Incorrect. Tadano: when making lifts at a load radius not shown, use the next longer radius. Never interpolate.

options.text: 30 ft — the shorter radius is always stronger
options.explanation: Incorrect. You do not take the shorter listed radius for an in-between job radius. Use the next longer listed radius.
Correct. Next longer listed radius is 35 ft. At 35 ft the 39.4 ft column is 27,500 lb (mode 1) / 26,900 lb (mode 2). Use that row, not a made-up 33 ft number.
Incorrect. 32.5 ft is the 0° boom-angle radius for 39.4 ft, not a substitute for a 33 ft working radius at a normal boom angle.

questions.question: The boom is between 39.4 ft and 53.7 ft and is not fully retracted. Which main-boom column do you use?

options.text: 39.4 ft — it is still shorter than 53.7 ft
options.explanation: Incorrect. 39.4 ft capacities are based on the boom fully retracted. If it is not fully retracted (and shorter than 53.7 ft), use the 53.7 ft capacities.
Correct. Tadano note: the 39.4 ft boom-length capacities are based on boom fully retracted. If not fully retracted [less than 53.7 ft], use the 53.7 ft boom-length capacities.

options.text: Average the 39.4 ft and 53.7 ft cells
options.explanation: Incorrect. Never average columns. When boom length is between listed values, use the next longer and next shorter booms for the same radius and take the lesser of the two — and the fully-retracted note still governs 39.4 ft.
Incorrect. Outrigger vs on-rubber is a different table, not a boom-length rule.

questions.question: Main-winch single line pull on this chart is 14,600 lb. What is the maximum load 6 parts of line can hoist, before the load chart is even considered?

options.explanation: Incorrect. That is one part.
Correct. 14,600 × 6 = 87,600 lb. Limited capacity = single line pull × parts of line. The load chart may be lower than this — the lesser governs.
Incorrect. 160,000 lb is a chart cell, not 6-part line pull.
Incorrect. That is 3 parts.

questions.question: During a boom lift the wind is 24 mph. The chart cell you read is 40,000 lb. What rated capacity does Tadano tell you to use?

options.text: 40,000 lb — wind is only a stop at 31 mph
options.explanation: Incorrect. Tadano reduces boom-lift capacity 50% from 20 mph (9 m/s) to 27 mph (12 m/s).

Correct. Rated lifting capacity is reduced by 50% when wind speed is 20–27 mph during boom lift. 40,000 × 0.5 = 20,000 lb. At 27–31 mph the reduction is 70%. At 31 mph or over, stop. Jib lift stops at 20 mph.
Incorrect. 70% reduction is the 27–31 mph band, not 24 mph.

options.text: 0 lb — any wind stops the lift
options.explanation: Incorrect. The stop is 31 mph on boom lift (20 mph on jib lift).
